title: Sphinganine inhibits macrophage polarization and protects against sepsis-induced intestinal injury.
authors: Chen, Yi-Fan; Wang, Ze-Tian; Zhao, Jian; Tang, Jian-Guo; Zhang, Bai-Yin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究鞘氨醇通过TLR2/NF-κB信号调控巨噬细胞极化保护脓毒症肠损伤，属纯湿实验与信号通路研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis-induced intestinal injury disrupts barrier function and exacerbates systemic inflammation, contributing to high mortality. AIM: To investigate the mechanism by which sphinganine protects against sepsis-induced intestinal injury, focusing on macrophage polarization and toll like receptor 2 (TLR2)/nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-kappaB) signaling. METHODS: A cecal ligation and puncture sepsis model was established in mice (n = 20/group). Treatments included sphinganine (15 mg/kg) and a TLR2 agonist [fibroblast-stimulating lipopeptide-1 (FSL-1), 10 mug/kg]. Serum markers [diamine oxidase (DAO), interleukin (IL)-1beta, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-alpha, IL-6] were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Intestinal injury and macrophage polarization [cluster of differentiation (CD) 86(+) M1, CD206(+) M2] were assessed via hematoxylin and eosin and immunofluorescence staining. Proteomic analysis, molecular docking, and Western blot were used to evaluate TLR2/NF-kappaB signaling. Data were analyzed by analysis of variance and t-test. RESULTS: Sphinganine significantly reduced serum levels of DAO (P < 0.05), IL-1beta, TNF-alpha, and IL-6 (P < 0.05), preserved intestinal crypt structure, and enhanced tight junction protein zonula occludens-1 expression. It promoted a shift from M1 (CD86(+)) to M2 (CD206(+)) macrophages. Proteomics identified TLR2 as the most differentially expressed protein, and molecular docking confirmed strong binding between sphinganine and TLR2 (-4.3 kcal/mol). Sphinganine downregulated TLR2 and phosphorylated-NF-kappaB p65 expression (P < 0.05), effects reversed by FSL-1. Total NF-kappaB p65 levels remained unchanged. CONCLUSION: Sphinganine protects against sepsis-induced intestinal injury by inhibiting TLR2/NF-kappaB signaling, modulating macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype, and preserving intestinal barrier integrity.
abstract_zh: 背景：脓毒症诱导的肠道损伤会破坏屏障功能并加剧全身炎症，导致高死亡率。目的：探讨鞘氨醇（sphinganine）保护脓毒症诱导肠道损伤的机制，重点关注巨噬细胞极化和Toll样受体2（TLR2）/核因子κB（NF-kappaB）信号通路。方法：在小鼠中建立盲肠结扎穿刺脓毒症模型（每组n = 20）。治疗包括鞘氨醇（15 mg/kg）和TLR2激动剂[成纤维细胞刺激脂肽-1（FSL-1），10 μg/kg]。通过酶联免疫吸附测定法测量血清标志物[二胺氧化酶（DAO）、白细胞介素（IL）-1β、肿瘤坏死因子（TNF）-α、IL-6]。通过苏木精-伊红染色和免疫荧光染色评估肠道损伤和巨噬细胞极化[分化簇（CD）86(+) M1、CD206(+) M2]。使用蛋白质组学分析、分子对接和Western blot评估TLR2/NF-kappaB信号通路。数据通过方差分析和t检验进行分析。结果：鞘氨醇显著降低血清DAO（P < 0.05）、IL-1β、TNF-α和IL-6水平（P < 0.05），保留肠道隐窝结构，并增强紧密连接蛋白zonula occludens-1的表达。它促进巨噬细胞从M1（CD86(+)）向M2（CD206(+)）表型转变。蛋白质组学鉴定TLR2为差异表达最显著的蛋白质，分子对接确认鞘氨醇与TLR2之间强结合（-4.3 kcal/mol）。鞘氨醇下调TLR2和磷酸化NF-kappaB p65表达（P < 0.05），这些效应被FSL-1逆转。总NF-kappaB p65水平保持不变。结论：鞘氨醇通过抑制TLR2/NF-kappaB信号通路、调节巨噬细胞向M2表型极化以及维持肠道屏障完整性，保护脓毒症诱导的肠道损伤。
